components.note: 耂 (a person bent with age, with long hair) — depicts an elderly figure.
匕 (here representing a cane or walking stick) — combined with the bent figure above, 老 pictures an old person leaning on a cane.
月, appearing twice side by side, originally depicted two people (or two strings of shells) together — giving 朋 its meaning 'friend, companion.'
又 (hand), shown twice and joined together — two hands clasped in friendship gave 友 its meaning 'friend.'
扌 (hand) — 指 relates to using the hand, specifically the fingers.
旨 (an aim, purpose) — combined with 扌 (hand), 指 came to mean 'finger' and 'to point,' aiming the hand at something.
军 (army) — an army being directed
扌 (hand) — the hand giving the command or wave
弓 (bow) — a strong bow that took great force to draw gave 强 its meaning 'strong, powerful.'
虫 was a different phonetic element historically; its pronunciation has shifted so far from qiáng over time that the sound link is no longer obvious.
士 (soldier) — 壮 describes someone as strong and robust, like a sturdy soldier.
丬 is only distantly related in sound to zhuàng — the connection has drifted apart to the point of being barely recognizable.
又 (hand) and 寸 (also derived from a hand shape) — together suggesting two hands matching or corresponding, related to 对's meaning 'correct, matching.'
力 (strength) — 劲 names physical strength or energy.
讠 (speech) — 认 relates to recognizing or acknowledging something, often expressed through words.
人 (rén) gives the sound — 认 is pronounced rèn, a close variant of the same sound.
屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
刂 (knife) — 制 relates to cutting and shaping, and by extension, to making or controlling something.
巾 (jīn) gives a hint of the sound — 制 is pronounced zhì, a connection that has drifted over time.
卩 (a person) — the one being dressed.
月 (a garment shape) — a hand 又 placing a coat on the person, giving 服 its meaning 'clothes; to obey, submit.'
土 (earth) — 坏 relates to something crumbling or deteriorating, like broken soil.
不 (bù) reflects an old phonetic link that has largely faded in the modern pronunciation huài.
屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
A picture of a nose; because people in ancient China would point to their own nose when referring to themselves, the character came to mean 'self.'
力 (strength/force) — 动 relates to movement produced by exertion or force.
氵 (water/stream) — water naturally follows a fixed course, an image linked to the idea of 'law' or 'method.'
去 (to go/a course) — the path a stream follows suggested a regulated, consistent way of doing things, hence 'law, method.'
阝 (a mound/enclosure) — relates to 院's meaning 'courtyard, institution,' an enclosed place.
完 (wán) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from yuàn.
西 is thought to depict a bird settling into its nest at dusk — since birds return to roost as the sun sets in the west, the character came to mean 'west.'
王 here is a variant of 玉 (jade), appearing once on each side of the character.
刂 (knife) — cutting a piece of jade in two, symbolizing a division into groups, gave 班 its meaning 'class, group.'
十 (here a straight vertical line) — 直 pictures something drawn perfectly straight.
目 (eye) — looking directly and steadily with the eye gave 直 its meaning 'straight' or 'direct.'
扌 (hand) — the hand doing the sowing.
番 (a field marked out into plots) — seeds scattered by hand across it, giving 播 its meaning 'to sow, to spread, to broadcast.'

meanings: (fig.) to have nothing further to do (with sb or sth)

components.note: 手 (hand), shown twice, side by side — two hands pressed together in a gesture of respect, giving 拜 its meaning 'to bow, to pay respects.'

meanings: to shift to an earlier date
to do sth ahead of time

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 提 relates to lifting or carrying something by hand.
是 (shì) gives a hint of the sound — 提 is pronounced tí, a connection that has shifted over time.
示 (an altar) — where offerings to ancestors are made
宀 (a roof) — the home where the family altar is kept
攵 (a hand with a stick) — 教 relates to instructing or disciplining, the traditional action of teaching.
孝 (xiào) gives a hint of the sound — 教 is pronounced jiào, a connection that has shifted somewhat.
虫 (worm, insect) — 蠢 originally described the wriggling movement of insects.
春 (chūn) gives the sound — an exact match with 蠢, differing only in tone.
贝 (shell/money) — 货 relates to goods that are bought and sold for money
化 (huà) gives a sound distantly related to 货's reading huò, having drifted apart over time
从 (two people, one following another) — depicts people together.
土 (earth/ground) — two people seated on the ground gave 坐 its meaning 'to sit.'
宀 (a roof) on top represents an enclosed structure.
牛 (cattle) below is the animal kept inside, giving 牢 its meaning 'pen, stable' and later 'prison.'

meanings: to take care that one does not

components.note: 扌 (hand) — suggests a gesture, a beckoning motion.
召 depicts a call or summons — a hand gesture calling someone over gave 招 its meaning 'to beckon, to recruit.'
口 (mouth) — 呼 describes an action of the mouth, such as calling out or breathing.
乎 (hū) gives the sound — an exact match with 呼.
山 (mountain) — 崩 describes a mountain or structure collapsing.
朋 (péng) gives a sound close to bēng, sharing the same rhyme and a related initial.
氵 (water) — 溃 originally described a river bursting its banks.
贵 (guì) gives the sound — a close match for kuì, sharing the same rhyme.
亻 (person) — 依 relates to a person relying or leaning on something
衣 (yī) gives the sound — 依 is also pronounced yī, an exact match
灬 (fire) — 然 originally described burning; the meaning later shifted to 'so, correct' as 然 became a grammatical particle.
肰 (rán) gives the sound — 然 is also pronounced rán, an exact match.
平 depicts a balance scale drawn level and symmetrical — a simple picture of flatness and equality.
青 (blue-green, nature) — 静 relates to a calm stillness, like still water or clear skies
争 (zhēng) gives a sound distantly related to 静's reading jìng, having drifted apart over time
辶 (walking/movement) — links 边's meaning to a boundary or edge one moves along.
臱 (biān) gives the sound — 边 is also pronounced biān, an exact match.
冂 (an enclosure or doorway) — 内 pictures the space one enters.
人 (person) — a person entering an enclosure gave 内 its meaning 'inside' or 'within.'
衤 (clothes) — 裤 names a piece of clothing, trousers.
库 (kù) gives the sound — an exact match with 裤.
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
冫 (water/ice) — 冲 relates to liquid, as in pouring or rinsing with water
中 (zhōng) gives a sound close to 冲's reading chōng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
氵 (water) — 浪 names movement on the surface of water, a wave.
良 (liáng) gives a rhyme close to làng, with a different initial and tone.
夕 (evening, night) — divination was traditionally done in the evening.
卜 (to divine, reading cracks in bone or shell) — combined with 夕 (evening), an evening divination was for unusual or 'outside' matters, giving 外 its meaning of 'outside' or 'foreign.'
大 (big, a person with arms and legs spread) pictures a person.
镸 (long) pictures a long piece of cloth wrapped around them, giving 套 its meaning 'cover, case.'
A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
口 (mouth) — 吓 relates to a shout or cry, as when someone is frightened.
下 (xià) gives the sound — an exact match with 吓.
土 (earth) — 坏 relates to something crumbling or deteriorating, like broken soil.
不 (bù) reflects an old phonetic link that has largely faded in the modern pronunciation huài.
阝 (a mound, related to terrain) — the ground where something happens.
臽 (a pit) — a hole in the ground, together giving 陷 its meaning 'to sink, to fall into a trap.'
入 depicts a simple wedge or arrow shape pointing inward, showing the direction of entering.
毛 (fur, hair) — 表 originally pictured a fur garment worn on the outside.
衣 (clothing) — an outer fur wrap gave 表 its meaning of 'outer' or 'surface,' and later, 'to express' (showing something on the surface).
回 depicts a spiral or winding shape — something that turns back on itself, giving rise to the meaning 'to return.'
扌 (hand) — 报 relates to taking action against someone.
卩 (a kneeling or bound person) — handling a wrongdoer and announcing the judgment gave 报 its meaning 'to report' or 'to announce.'
氵 (water) — 演 originally described water flowing and spreading out, later extended to 'developing, unfolding'
寅 (yín) gives a sound distantly related to 演's reading yǎn, having drifted apart over time
讠 (speech) — 讲 relates to speaking, explaining, telling
井 (jǐng) gives a sound close to 讲's reading jiǎng
我 (wǒ) reflects the character's phonetic root, though the sound has diverged over time from the modern reading é.
囗 (a boundary/enclosure) surrounding 玉 (jade, treasure) — a country pictured as protected, valuable territory.
广 (a building/shelter) — 底 relates to the base or bottom, as of a structure
氐 (dǐ) gives the sound — 底 is also pronounced dǐ, an exact match
A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.
宀 (a roof) — the shelter of a house.
且 here representing an altar or memorial tablet, together suggesting a fitting, proper ceremony held at home, giving 宜 its meaning 'suitable, fitting.'
日 (sun/day) — relates to 时's meaning of 'time, season'; the phonetic part of the character was later replaced by 寸 in the simplified form

meanings: (of a shop etc) to close (for the night or permanently)

components.note: 门 is a picture of a double-leafed door or gate, drawn symmetrically to show two swinging panels.
纟 (silk/thread) — 经 originally referred to the vertical warp threads in weaving.
工 (gōng) gives a related sound cue for 经 (jīng), reflecting an older, closer pronunciation link between the two.
纟 (thread) — 纪 relates to organizing threads in order, extended to mean 'record, era'
己 (jǐ) gives a sound close to 纪's reading jì
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
亻 (person) — 停 relates to a person coming to a halt
亭 (tíng) gives the sound — an exact match with 停's reading tíng
A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'
土 (earth) — 场 relates to a flat open area of ground, such as a field or venue.
昜 (yáng) gives a hint of the sound — 场 is pronounced chǎng, a connection that has drifted significantly over time.
刂 (knife) — 判 originally related to cutting something apart to distinguish or decide
半 (bàn) gives a sound close to 判's reading pàn, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
斤 (an axe) — cutting through something.
米 (grain, in the simplified form; a bundle of thread in the traditional 斷) — the material being cut, giving 断 its meaning 'to break off, cut, sever.'
长 (simplified from 長) depicts an elderly figure with long flowing hair and a cane — length and seniority are linked in the original picture.
讠 (speech) — 试 relates to proposing or trying something out
式 (shì) gives the sound — an exact match with 试's pronunciation shì
马 (horse) — 验 originally related to examining or testing horses, later extended to 'to test, examine, verify'
佥 (qiān) gives a loose sound connection to 验's reading yàn
丹 depicts a pellet of red cinnabar mineral, dug from a mine — the source of its meaning 'cinnabar, red, pellet.'
亻 (person) — 做 relates to a person carrying out an action.
故 (cause, reason, to happen) — combined with 亻 (person), 做 came to mean 'to make' or 'to do,' someone actively causing something to happen.
林 here depicts eyes shut in sleep, not its usual meaning 'forest.'
夕 (evening, night) — sleeping at night is when dreams occur, giving 梦 its meaning 'dream.'
母 (mǔ, 'mother') serves as the phonetic base; the sound has since diverged from měi, so the connection is mostly historical today.
干 (originally a person) shown carrying a heavy load of grain on their back — since harvests came once a year, the character came to mean 'year.'
女 (woman) — 奶 relates to a woman nursing, and to milk.
乃 (nǎi) is an exact match for the sound of 奶.
酉 (originally 'wine jar,' broadened to fermented foods) — 酪 names fermented dairy products like cheese and koumiss.
各 (gè) is the phonetic element from the character's history, but its modern reading no longer resembles 酪's lào — the connection today is historical rather than audible.
阝 (mound, place) marks a location.
百 (hundred, many) sits beside it — a large, unfamiliar place, giving 陌 its meaning as a raised path between fields, and later, its role in 陌生 ('unfamiliar').
屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
氵 (water) — the water that is deep.
罙 (deep) — combined with water, giving 深 its meaning 'deep.'
刂 (a knife) — 刻 relates to carving with a blade
亥 (hài) is the historical phonetic element; it no longer closely matches 刻's modern reading kè
⺮ (bamboo) — 管 originally referred to a bamboo pipe or tube, later broadening to mean 'to manage' or 'to control.'
官 (guān) gives a hint of the sound — 管 is pronounced guǎn, a connection that has shifted only slightly in tone.
土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'
A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.
宀 (roof) — 室 refers to an enclosed room under a roof
至 (zhì) gives the sound — an exact match with 室's reading shì
